## Avaliação do poder preditivo

### Nested CV 10-folds

```{r}
## =================================================================
## NESTED cluster-respecting K-fold CV for the national multinomial model
## LASSO variable selection is re-run INSIDE each training fold (not fixed
## up front), then the multinomial model is refit on the selected variables
## and evaluated on the held-out fold. Evaluation metric: survey-weighted
## macro-F1.
## =================================================================
## COST WARNING: this is the expensive nested-CV path discussed earlier --
## each outer fold now also runs cv.glmnet's own internal CV to pick lambda.
## With K outer folds x inner_nfolds internal folds, expect roughly K times
## the cost of a single cv.glmnet + vglm run, not the ~1-minute flat-CV cost.
## Time a single fold first (see USAGE at the bottom) before running all K.
##
## Assumes: pnadc_rebalanced_complete (svyrep.design, pweights/repweights
## already balanced+anchored), VGAM/survey/glmnet packages loaded, and
## `regression_variables` (character vector of candidate predictor names,
## as in create_matrix_national()) defined.

library(VGAM)
library(survey)
library(glmnet)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Lasso-selection helpers (carried over from pipeline.txt, needed here
#    because selection now happens inside each fold rather than once
#    up front)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
get_selected_vars <- function(coefs) {
  selected_vars <- c()
  for (i in seq_along(coefs)) {
    matriz_coef <- coefs[[i]]
    active_name <- rownames(matriz_coef)[which(matriz_coef != 0)]
    selected_vars <- c(selected_vars, active_name)
  }
  final_vars <- unique(selected_vars)
  final_vars <- final_vars[final_vars != "(Intercept)"]
  final_vars
}

clean_lasso_names <- function(matrix, variables) {
  clean_vector <- c()
  for (matrix_name in matrix) {
    for (orig_var in variables) {
      if (startsWith(matrix_name, orig_var)) {
        clean_vector <- c(clean_vector, orig_var)
        break
      }
    }
  }
  unique(clean_vector)
}

create_formula <- function(y, x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    # LASSO selected nothing in this fold -- fall back to intercept-only
    # rather than erroring on paste(character(0)). Worth flagging if this
    # ever triggers: it means this fold's training data couldn't support
    # any predictor surviving regularization.
    warning("No variables selected -- falling back to intercept-only formula.")
    return(as.formula(paste(y, "~ 1")))
  }
  right_side <- paste(x, collapse = " + ")
  as.formula(paste(y, "~", right_side))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Cluster-respecting fold assignment (unchanged from flat-CV version)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
create_cluster_folds <- function(design_obj, cluster_var, k = 10, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  cluster_ids <- design_obj$variables[[cluster_var]]
  unique_clusters <- unique(cluster_ids)
  unique_clusters <- sample(unique_clusters)
  
  fold_assignment <- rep(1:k, length.out = length(unique_clusters))
  cluster_to_fold  <- setNames(fold_assignment, as.character(unique_clusters))
  
  row_fold <- unname(cluster_to_fold[as.character(cluster_ids)])
  print(table(row_fold))
  
  return(row_fold)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Survey-weighted precision, recall, and F1 per class (unchanged)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
weighted_class_metrics <- function(y_true, y_pred, w, levels_all) {
  y_true <- factor(y_true, levels = levels_all)
  y_pred <- factor(y_pred, levels = levels_all)
  
  out <- data.frame(
    class     = levels_all,
    precision = NA_real_,
    recall    = NA_real_,
    f1        = NA_real_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (i in seq_along(levels_all)) {
    cl <- levels_all[i]
    tp <- sum(w[y_true == cl & y_pred == cl])
    fp <- sum(w[y_true != cl & y_pred == cl])
    fn <- sum(w[y_true == cl & y_pred != cl])
    
    precision <- if ((tp + fp) > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else 0
    recall    <- if ((tp + fn) > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else 0
    f1 <- if ((precision + recall) > 0) {
      2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
    } else 0
    
    out$precision[i] <- precision
    out$recall[i]     <- recall
    out$f1[i]          <- f1
  }
  
  out
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2c. Survey-weighted confusion matrix
#     Cells are SUMS OF WEIGHTS (i.e. population-scale, not raw row
#     counts), consistent with the rest of this pipeline. Explicitly
#     stripped to a plain numeric matrix -- xtabs()/table() return a
#     "table"-classed object, and this pipeline has already been bitten
#     once by a silently persisting "table" class corrupting downstream
#     arithmetic (see rebalance_weights_national()).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
build_weighted_confusion_matrix <- function(y_true, y_pred, w, levels_all) {
  y_true <- factor(y_true, levels = levels_all)
  y_pred <- factor(y_pred, levels = levels_all)
  
  cm <- matrix(0, nrow = length(levels_all), ncol = length(levels_all),
               dimnames = list(true = levels_all, predicted = levels_all))
  
  for (i in seq_along(levels_all)) {
    for (j in seq_along(levels_all)) {
      cm[i, j] <- sum(w[y_true == levels_all[i] & y_pred == levels_all[j]])
    }
  }
  
  cm  # plain numeric matrix, population-weighted counts
}

# Row-normalized version: each row sums to 100, showing what share of the
# TRUE population in each category was predicted into each category
# (diagonal = recall, in percentage-of-population terms).
row_normalize_confusion_matrix <- function(cm) {
  pct <- sweep(cm, 1, rowSums(cm), FUN = "/") * 100
  as.matrix(pct)  # defensive strip, same reasoning as above
}


#     Computed ONCE from the full dataset, before any splitting. This
#     guarantees model.matrix() produces the same dummy columns in every
#     fold (even if a level has zero rows in a given training fold) and
#     that vglm's predict() never meets an unseen factor level in a test
#     fold.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
force_factor_levels <- function(df, vars) {
  level_map <- list()
  for (v in vars) {
    if (is.character(df[[v]]) || is.factor(df[[v]])) {
      level_map[[v]] <- levels(factor(df[[v]]))
    }
  }
  level_map
}

apply_factor_levels <- function(df, level_map) {
  for (v in names(level_map)) {
    df[[v]] <- factor(df[[v]], levels = level_map[[v]])
  }
  df
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Single fold, NESTED: run LASSO selection on the training fold only,
#    refit multinomial on the selected variables, predict on the held-out
#    fold.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
run_fold_nested <- function(fold_i, row_fold, df, regression_variables,
                            weight_var, y_var, levels_all, seed,
                            inner_nfolds = 10) {
  
  train_idx <- which(row_fold != fold_i)
  test_idx  <- which(row_fold == fold_i)
  
  train_df <- df[train_idx, ]
  test_df  <- df[test_idx, ]
  
  train_df$.wt <- train_df[[weight_var]]
  test_df$.wt  <- test_df[[weight_var]]
  
  train_df[[y_var]] <- factor(train_df[[y_var]], levels = levels_all)
  test_df[[y_var]]  <- factor(test_df[[y_var]],  levels = levels_all)
  
  # ---- Step A: LASSO variable selection, using ONLY this fold's training
  #      data. This is what makes it "nested" -- the inner cv.glmnet call
  #      below never sees this fold's held-out rows.
  X_matrix <- tryCatch(
    model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = train_df[, regression_variables, drop = FALSE]),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  if (inherits(X_matrix, "error")) {
    warning(sprintf("Fold %d: failed to build design matrix: %s",
                    fold_i, conditionMessage(X_matrix)))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  set.seed(seed + fold_i)  # reproducible inner CV per fold
  lasso_fit <- tryCatch(
    glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      x = X_matrix,
      y = train_df[[y_var]],
      family  = "multinomial",
      weights = train_df$.wt,
      nfolds  = inner_nfolds
    ),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  if (inherits(lasso_fit, "error")) {
    warning(sprintf("Fold %d: LASSO failed to fit: %s", fold_i, conditionMessage(lasso_fit)))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # lambda.1se instead of lambda.min: picks the most parsimonious model
  # within one standard error of the minimum CV deviance, trading a
  # small amount of fit for a sparser, more stable selection -- Friedman,
  # Hastie & Tibshirani (2010) recommend this as the default choice when
  # parsimony is preferred over chasing the minimum-error lambda exactly.
  coefs <- coef(lasso_fit, s = "lambda.1se")
  selected_raw   <- get_selected_vars(coefs)
  selected_clean <- clean_lasso_names(selected_raw, regression_variables)
  
  fold_formula <- create_formula(y_var, selected_clean)
  
  # ---- Step B: refit multinomial on ONLY the variables selected in this
  #      fold's training data, then predict on the held-out fold.
  fit <- tryCatch(
    VGAM::vglm(fold_formula, data = train_df, weights = .wt,
               family = VGAM::multinomial(refLevel = 1)),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    warning(sprintf("Fold %d: vglm refit failed to converge: %s",
                    fold_i, conditionMessage(fit)))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  pred_probs <- VGAM::predictvglm(fit, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
  
  # Same caveat as the flat-CV version: verify colnames(pred_probs) matches
  # levels_all order on your first real run.
  if (is.null(dim(pred_probs))) {
    # Intercept-only / single-category edge case: predictvglm can return
    # a vector instead of a matrix. Handle defensively rather than crash.
    pred_class <- rep(levels_all[1], nrow(test_df))
  } else {
    pred_class <- levels_all[apply(pred_probs, 1, which.max)]
  }
  
  class_metrics <- weighted_class_metrics(
    y_true     = test_df[[y_var]],
    y_pred     = pred_class,
    w          = test_df$.wt,
    levels_all = levels_all
  )
  
  list(
    fold           = fold_i,
    n_train        = nrow(train_df),
    n_test         = nrow(test_df),
    selected_vars  = selected_clean,
    lambda_1se     = lasso_fit$lambda.1se,
    macro_f1       = mean(class_metrics$f1),
    class_metrics  = class_metrics,
    # Raw test-set predictions, kept so they can be pooled across all K
    # folds afterward to build one full-sample confusion matrix -- every
    # observation is a test-set member in exactly one fold, so pooling
    # reconstructs a complete out-of-sample confusion matrix.
    y_true         = as.character(test_df[[y_var]]),
    y_pred         = pred_class,
    w              = test_df$.wt
  )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Full nested pipeline -- national model, no macroregion split
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
run_nested_cv_national <- function(design_obj, regression_variables, cluster_var,
                                   y_var = "tenure_condition",
                                   k = 10, seed = 123, inner_nfolds = 10) {
  
  df <- design_obj$variables
  weight_var <- ".sampling_weight"
  df[[weight_var]] <- as.vector(weights(design_obj, "sampling"))  # strip any "table" class
  
  levels_all <- levels(factor(df[[y_var]]))
  
  # Force consistent factor levels on all candidate predictors up front,
  # from the FULL dataset -- see note on force_factor_levels() above.
  level_map <- force_factor_levels(df, regression_variables)
  df <- apply_factor_levels(df, level_map)
  
  row_fold <- create_cluster_folds(design_obj, cluster_var, k = k, seed = seed)
  
  fold_results <- vector("list", k)
  for (i in seq_len(k)) {
    message(sprintf("Running NESTED fold %d/%d (LASSO + refit)...", i, k))
    fold_results[[i]] <- run_fold_nested(
      fold_i = i, row_fold = row_fold, df = df,
      regression_variables = regression_variables,
      weight_var = weight_var, y_var = y_var, levels_all = levels_all,
      seed = seed, inner_nfolds = inner_nfolds
    )
  }
  
  fold_results <- Filter(Negate(is.null), fold_results)
  if (length(fold_results) < k) {
    warning(sprintf("%d of %d folds failed and were dropped -- see warnings above.",
                    k - length(fold_results), k))
  }
  if (length(fold_results) == 0) {
    stop("All folds failed -- see warnings above for the underlying error(s).")
  }
  
  macro_f1_by_fold <- sapply(fold_results, function(x) x$macro_f1)
  
  # ---- Per-category precision/recall/F1 table, as in the flat-CV version
  all_class_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fold_results, function(x) {
    cbind(fold = x$fold, x$class_metrics)
  }))
  class_table <- aggregate(cbind(precision, recall, f1) ~ class,
                           data = all_class_metrics, FUN = mean)
  class_table_sd <- aggregate(cbind(precision, recall, f1) ~ class,
                              data = all_class_metrics, FUN = sd)
  names(class_table_sd)[-1] <- paste0(names(class_table_sd)[-1], "_sd")
  class_table <- merge(class_table, class_table_sd, by = "class")
  class_table <- class_table[match(levels_all, class_table$class), ]
  rownames(class_table) <- NULL
  
  # ---- Variable-selection stability across folds: this is the natural
  #      byproduct of nesting the selection step, and worth reporting --
  #      it shows how sensitive the LASSO selection was to which 90% of
  #      the data it saw.
  all_selected <- unlist(lapply(fold_results, function(x) x$selected_vars))
  selection_freq <- as.data.frame(table(all_selected))
  names(selection_freq) <- c("variable", "times_selected")
  selection_freq$out_of_k <- length(fold_results)
  selection_freq <- selection_freq[order(-selection_freq$times_selected), ]
  rownames(selection_freq) <- NULL
  
  # ---- Pooled out-of-sample confusion matrix, built from EVERY fold's
  #      held-out predictions concatenated together -- i.e. covers the
  #      full sample, entirely out-of-sample, with no observation counted
  #      more than once. Only valid if no folds were dropped above; if
  #      some failed, this covers only the successful folds' rows.
  pooled_y_true <- unlist(lapply(fold_results, function(x) x$y_true))
  pooled_y_pred <- unlist(lapply(fold_results, function(x) x$y_pred))
  pooled_w      <- unlist(lapply(fold_results, function(x) x$w))
  
  confusion_matrix     <- build_weighted_confusion_matrix(
    pooled_y_true, pooled_y_pred, pooled_w, levels_all
  )
  confusion_matrix_pct <- row_normalize_confusion_matrix(confusion_matrix)
  
  list(
    mean_macro_f1        = mean(macro_f1_by_fold),
    sd_macro_f1          = sd(macro_f1_by_fold),
    per_fold             = macro_f1_by_fold,
    class_table          = class_table,
    selection_freq       = selection_freq,
    confusion_matrix     = confusion_matrix,      # population-weighted counts
    confusion_matrix_pct = confusion_matrix_pct,  # row-normalized, % of true population
    fold_details         = fold_results
  )
}
```

```{r}
## =================================================================
## Heatmap-style confusion matrix -- both raw population counts and
## row-normalized percentages, sized larger so long category labels
## (e.g. "proprietario_formal") and multi-digit numbers don't overlap.
## =================================================================
## build_weighted_confusion_matrix() returns a PLAIN matrix (deliberately
## stripped of "table" class -- see its own comments for why), so
## as.data.frame() on it does NOT give a long-format Observed/Predicted/
## Freq frame directly. Built explicitly below instead.

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Reusable plotting function -- takes either confusion_matrix (raw
# counts) or confusion_matrix_pct (row-normalized), toggled by is_percent.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
plot_confusion_matrix <- function(cm, is_percent = FALSE, title = NULL) {
  
  cm_df <- data.frame(
    # as.vector(cm) unrolls column-by-column (R is column-major), so
    # Observed must cycle through rownames fastest (times = ncol) and
    # Predicted must repeat each colname consecutively (each = nrow).
    Observed  = factor(rep(rownames(cm), times = ncol(cm)), levels = rownames(cm)),
    Predicted = factor(rep(colnames(cm), each  = nrow(cm)), levels = colnames(cm)),
    Freq      = as.vector(cm)
  )
  
  if (is_percent) {
    cm_df$label <- paste0(format(round(cm_df$Freq, 1), decimal.mark = ",", nsmall = 1), "%")
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                                       labels = label_number(suffix = "%"))
  } else {
    cm_df$label <- format(round(cm_df$Freq, 0), big.mark = ".")
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                                       labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"))
  }
  
  ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Observed, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = label, color = Freq > (max(Freq) / 2)),
      size = 6.5   # bigger text so multi-digit numbers fit and read clearly
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "black"), guide = "none") +
    fill_scale +
    # Reverse row order so the first row of the matrix plots at the TOP.
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(rownames(cm))) +
    labs(x = "Categoria prevista", y = "Categoria observada", fill = "", title = title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 24) +   # bigger base size -> bigger axis text/titles
    theme(
      panel.grid   = element_blank(),
      axis.text    = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
      axis.title   = element_text(size = 14, face = "plain"),
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0.5),
      legend.position = "right",
      # Extra margin so long category names (e.g. "proprietario_formal")
      # never get clipped against the plot edge.
      plot.margin  = margin(t = 15, r = 15, b = 15, l = 15)
    )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Build both versions
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
p_counts  <- plot_confusion_matrix(nested_cv_results$confusion_matrix,
                                   is_percent = FALSE,
                                   title = "Matriz de confusão -- população total")

p_percent <- plot_confusion_matrix(nested_cv_results$confusion_matrix_pct,
                                   is_percent = TRUE,
                                   title = "Matriz de confusão -- % da categoria observada")

ggsave("../outputs/confusion_matrix_counts.png",  p_counts,  width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave("../outputs/confusion_matrix_percent.png", p_percent, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Post-LASSO

### Tarefa 1: Interpretação

```{r}
# Extract the raw summary object
mod_sum <- summary(post_lasso_national)

# Search for the matrix
if ("coeftable" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coeftable
} else if ("coefficients" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coefficients
} else if ("coef3" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coef3
} else {
  raw_matrix <- as.matrix(mod_sum)
}

# Get categories
all_levels <- pnadc$variables$tenure_condition
estimated_levels <- all_levels[-1]

clean_df <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(raw_matrix),
  Estimate_B = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 1]),
  Std_Error = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 2]),
  Wald_z = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 3]),
  Sig = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 4]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Clean the text, Map Categories, and calculate Odds Ratio
clean_df$Variable <- sub(":.*", "", clean_df$Term)
clean_df$Eq_Index <- as.numeric(sub(".*:", "", clean_df$Term))
clean_df$Equation <- estimated_levels[clean_df$Eq_Index]
clean_df$Exp_B <- exp(clean_df$Estimate_B)

# Order the columns exactly as needed
final_data <- clean_df[, c("Equation", "Variable", "Estimate_B", "Std_Error", "Wald_z", "Sig", "Exp_B")]

# Render table
final_table <- final_data %>%
  group_by(Equation) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    Estimate_B = "Estimate B",
    Std_Error = "Std. error",
    Wald_z = "Wald",
    Sig = "Sig.",
    Exp_B = "Exp(B)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Estimate_B, Std_Error, Wald_z, Sig, Exp_B),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Sig, rows = Sig < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**TABLE 4**"),
    subtitle = "Multinomial logit model tenure choice"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.background.color = "#f0f0f0",
    table.border.top.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table_body.hlines.color = "lightgray"
  )

final_table
```

### Tarefa 2: previsão

```{r}
## =================================================================
## Cluster-respecting K-fold CV for the national multinomial model
## Evaluation metric: survey-weighted macro-F1
## =================================================================
## Assumes: pnadc_rebalanced_complete (svyrep.design, pweights/repweights
## already balanced+anchored), formula_national (from create_formula()),
## and VGAM/survey packages loaded.

library(VGAM)
library(survey)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Cluster-respecting fold assignment
#    Whole clusters (not individual rows) are assigned to folds, so
#    no cluster ever has members split across train and test.
#    IMPORTANT: cluster_var should be the finest unit where correlation
#    between observations is strongest (typically household id).
#    If your design only carries a PSU-level id (e.g. "UPA"), that's a
#    safer/coarser fallback, but prefer a household-level id if you
#    have one -- PSU-level splitting can still leak household-level
#    correlation across train/test.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
create_cluster_folds <- function(design_obj, cluster_var, k = 10, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  cluster_ids <- design_obj$variables[[cluster_var]]
  unique_clusters <- unique(cluster_ids)
  unique_clusters <- sample(unique_clusters)  # shuffle order before assigning
  
  fold_assignment <- rep(1:k, length.out = length(unique_clusters))
  cluster_to_fold  <- setNames(fold_assignment, as.character(unique_clusters))
  
  row_fold <- unname(cluster_to_fold[as.character(cluster_ids)])
  
  # Quick diagnostic: row counts per fold. Uneven cluster sizes (PSUs/
  # households vary a lot in PNAD) can make folds unequal in row count
  # even though they're equal in cluster count -- worth eyeballing.
  print(table(row_fold))
  
  return(row_fold)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Survey-weighted precision, recall, and F1 -- per class
#    TP/FP/FN are computed as SUMS OF WEIGHTS, not raw row counts,
#    consistent with treating each observation as representing its
#    survey weight's worth of the population.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
weighted_class_metrics <- function(y_true, y_pred, w, levels_all) {
  y_true <- factor(y_true, levels = levels_all)
  y_pred <- factor(y_pred, levels = levels_all)
  
  out <- data.frame(
    class     = levels_all,
    precision = NA_real_,
    recall    = NA_real_,
    f1        = NA_real_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (i in seq_along(levels_all)) {
    cl <- levels_all[i]
    tp <- sum(w[y_true == cl & y_pred == cl])
    fp <- sum(w[y_true != cl & y_pred == cl])
    fn <- sum(w[y_true == cl & y_pred != cl])
    
    precision <- if ((tp + fp) > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else 0
    recall    <- if ((tp + fn) > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else 0
    f1 <- if ((precision + recall) > 0) {
      2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
    } else 0
    
    out$precision[i] <- precision
    out$recall[i]     <- recall
    out$f1[i]          <- f1
  }
  
  out
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Single fold: train on K-1 clusters, predict on the held-out fold
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
run_fold <- function(fold_i, row_fold, df, formula, weight_var, y_var, levels_all) {
  
  train_idx <- which(row_fold != fold_i)
  test_idx  <- which(row_fold == fold_i)
  
  train_df <- df[train_idx, ]
  test_df  <- df[test_idx, ]
  
  # Attach the weight as a column of the data frame itself, under a fixed
  # name, and reference THAT column in weights= below. Passing a bare
  # local variable (e.g. weights = train_w) is unreliable here: vglm()'s
  # internal non-standard evaluation of `weights` doesn't reliably resolve
  # a loose variable across the extra call-stack layers introduced by
  # calling it from inside run_fold() inside a loop inside tryCatch().
  # Putting it in `data=` sidesteps that entirely -- data is evaluated
  # normally, not via frame-walking.
  train_df$.wt <- train_df[[weight_var]]
  test_df$.wt  <- test_df[[weight_var]]
  
  # Force the SAME full level set on both sides. If a category truly
  # has zero training rows in this fold, vglm cannot estimate a
  # coefficient for it -- fit will error and this fold is skipped
  # (see tryCatch below). Worth checking per_class counts if that happens.
  train_df[[y_var]] <- factor(train_df[[y_var]], levels = levels_all)
  test_df[[y_var]]  <- factor(test_df[[y_var]],  levels = levels_all)
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    VGAM::vglm(formula, data = train_df, weights = .wt,
               family = VGAM::multinomial(refLevel = 1)),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    warning(sprintf("Fold %d failed to converge: %s", fold_i, conditionMessage(fit)))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  pred_probs <- VGAM::predictvglm(fit, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
  
  # SANITY CHECK worth running once manually: confirm colnames(pred_probs)
  # follows the same order as levels_all. VGAM's multinomial() column
  # order can differ from plain factor level order in some setups.
  pred_class <- levels_all[apply(pred_probs, 1, which.max)]
  
  class_metrics <- weighted_class_metrics(
    y_true     = test_df[[y_var]],
    y_pred     = pred_class,
    w          = test_df$.wt,
    levels_all = levels_all
  )
  
  list(
    fold          = fold_i,
    n_train       = nrow(train_df),
    n_test        = nrow(test_df),
    macro_f1      = mean(class_metrics$f1),
    class_metrics = class_metrics
  )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Full pipeline -- national model, no macroregion split
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
run_cv_national <- function(design_obj, formula, cluster_var,
                            y_var = "tenure_condition",
                            k = 10, seed = 123) {
  
  df <- design_obj$variables
  weight_var <- ".sampling_weight"
  df[[weight_var]] <- weights(design_obj, "sampling")
  
  # Guard against the class/dim bug from earlier in this pipeline --
  # strip class/dim defensively in case an upstream weight column
  # still carries a "table" class.
  df[[weight_var]] <- as.vector(df[[weight_var]])
  
  levels_all <- levels(factor(df[[y_var]]))
  
  row_fold <- create_cluster_folds(design_obj, cluster_var, k = k, seed = seed)
  
  fold_results <- vector("list", k)
  for (i in seq_len(k)) {
    message(sprintf("Running fold %d/%d...", i, k))
    fold_results[[i]] <- run_fold(
      fold_i = i, row_fold = row_fold, df = df,
      formula = formula, weight_var = weight_var,
      y_var = y_var, levels_all = levels_all
    )
  }
  
  fold_results <- Filter(Negate(is.null), fold_results)
  if (length(fold_results) < k) {
    warning(sprintf("%d of %d folds failed and were dropped -- see warnings above.",
                    k - length(fold_results), k))
  }
  # Fail loudly and clearly if every fold failed, rather than letting an
  # empty list silently break sapply()/sd() downstream with an opaque
  # "is.atomic(x) is not TRUE" error.
  if (length(fold_results) == 0) {
    stop("All folds failed -- see warnings above for the underlying error(s).")
  }
  
  macro_f1_by_fold <- sapply(fold_results, function(x) x$macro_f1)
  
  # ---- Per-category table: mean (and SD) of precision/recall/F1 across
  #      the K folds, one row per tenure_condition category. This is the
  #      table to report alongside the headline macro-F1.
  all_class_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fold_results, function(x) {
    cbind(fold = x$fold, x$class_metrics)
  }))
  
  class_table <- aggregate(
    cbind(precision, recall, f1) ~ class,
    data = all_class_metrics,
    FUN  = mean
  )
  class_table_sd <- aggregate(
    cbind(precision, recall, f1) ~ class,
    data = all_class_metrics,
    FUN  = sd
  )
  names(class_table_sd)[-1] <- paste0(names(class_table_sd)[-1], "_sd")
  class_table <- merge(class_table, class_table_sd, by = "class")
  
  # Keep original category order (aggregate()/merge() alphabetizes by default)
  class_table <- class_table[match(levels_all, class_table$class), ]
  rownames(class_table) <- NULL
  
  list(
    mean_macro_f1 = mean(macro_f1_by_fold),
    sd_macro_f1   = sd(macro_f1_by_fold),
    per_fold      = macro_f1_by_fold,
    class_table   = class_table,
    fold_details  = fold_results
  )
}
```

```{r}

   design_obj  = pnadc_rebalanced_complete,
   formula     = formula_national,
   cluster_var = "UPA",   # <-- replace with your actual household/PSU id column
   k = 10
 )

cv_results$mean_macro_f1   # headline number to report/compare across the 6 models
cv_results$sd_macro_f1     # spread across folds -- worth reporting too
cv_results$per_fold
cv_results$class_table     # per-category precision / recall / F1, mean +/- SD across folds

knitr::kable(cv_results$class_table, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# 1. Calculate precision: diagonal (correct predictions) divided by row sums (total predictions per category)
precision_values <- diag(weighted_confusion_matrix) / rowSums(weighted_confusion_matrix)

# Handle potential NaN values if a category was never predicted (row sum = 0)
precision_values[is.na(precision_values)] <- 0

# 2. Convert to percentage and round to 1 decimal place
precision_percent <- round(precision_values * 100, 1)

# 3. Create a clean summary data frame
precision_table <- data.frame(
  Categoria = names(precision_percent),
  Precisao_Pct = paste0(precision_percent, "%"),
  Valores_Exatos = precision_percent
)

print("Precisão (% de acertos das previsões) por Categoria:")
print(precision_table)
```
